exportPreflight.note: This exact recipe converted successfully on this rig. Counts describe the generated local KeyframeSequence; this does not publish or guarantee visual quality.

advisories.detail: Head, LeftFoot, LeftHand, LeftLowerArm, LeftLowerLeg, LeftUpperArm, LeftUpperLeg, LowerTorso, RightFoot, RightHand, RightLowerArm, RightLowerLeg, RightUpperArm, RightUpperLeg, UpperTorso has more than 32 keys. Check for redundant keys and preserve only keys that shape timing, arcs, contacts, or secondary motion.
Every track uses the same key times. Check whether the whole body is moving in lockstep; stagger motion by role where the action calls for it.

Preview the motion on the target rig. Judge silhouette, readable intent, weight shifts, contacts, arcs, spacing, and transitions. Numeric trackMotion values are finite differences of local recipe keys (not rendered/world-space measurements) and can highlight intervals to inspect, but cannot certify animation quality.

coordination.basis: Independent base-track local channels only. Enabled/disabled layers and root motion remain separately reported and are not composed here; no hierarchy or world-space inference is made.

composedCoordination.basis: Composed local joint trajectories sampled after base tracks, enabled weighted layers in stack order, and matching root-motion channels. Disabled and zero-weight layers are excluded. This is resultant local motion, not per-source attribution; it does not infer hierarchy, world-space travel, rendered quality, or intent.

actionPhaseMap.markerRule: Explicit marker.phase metadata takes precedence: anticipation, main_action, follow_through, and recovery label boundaries; event excludes the marker from phase segmentation. For legacy markers with no phase field, recognized names (anticipation/windup/preparation, action/attack/strike/impact/release/cast, follow-through, recovery/settle/return) retain name-based inference. Ordinary events can use phase:event to disambiguate a phase-like name. Without any recognized phase marker, the full clip is returned as unsegmented; intent is not inferred from motion peaks.

poseProgression.basis: Composed local joint transforms sampled from base tracks, enabled weighted layers in stack order, and matching root-motion tracks. Rotation uses quaternion angular distance. No parent hierarchy, world-space trajectory, rendered appearance, or physical contact is inferred.

interpretation.signalMeaning: Local pose change per second; a high value may be intentional for a fast action.
interpretation.evidenceScope: Sampled at 145 evaluations over the authored base channel using local recipe transforms and the recorded outgoing easing. It excludes rig hierarchy, skinning, world-space motion, physics, and rendered appearance.

audit.limitation: Structural advisories and kinematic measurements cannot certify an artistic result or claim that the animation was visually inspected. trackMotion uses key-to-key finite differences; curveMotion samples the authored easing and shortest-path quaternion interpolation at the requested rate plus every key time, then estimates derivatives by finite differences. Both operate in local recipe coordinates and exclude rig hierarchy, skinning, rendered/world-space motion, and collision/physics.
audit.next: Review contactTrackCoverage for each declared interval. no_matching_channel and inactive_channels_only are authoring cues, not automatic failures: a resting effector may need no authored channel, while an active channel does not prove contact. For rig compatibility, rerun this audit with sessionId and rigId from a fresh inspection; offline channel matching cannot establish that the effector exists or is driven on the target rig. Preview and inspect the animation before making quality claims.

rigCoverage.limitation: Coverage uses exact target names or the caller-supplied jointMap; it does not infer semantic body roles. Unmapped names remain unresolved; inactive channels are disclosed but excluded. Contact coverage identifies rig-node/channel availability only and cannot prove support, grip, collision, or visible contact.

semanticRoleCoverage.limitation: Role resolution uses exact R6/R15 naming conventions, explicitly caller-confirmed exact driven-joint mappings, or a unique joint-name token match labeled inferred; inferred roles require review. Caller-confirmed mapping is not anatomical truth. It uses no mesh, position, axes, anatomy, or joint-limit evidence. Role counts may share one driven joint (especially R6 arm/hand and leg/foot aliases), and absent or inactive roles are not failures: intentional stillness is valid. This is coverage context, not a quality score or quota.
